about: The `table_semantics` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS account
rows.what_it_answers: The chart of accounts — no money at all. One row per MUNIS account number split into fund, department, org and object, with its DESE function code, its name, whether it is revenue or expense, whether it is a roll-up or a detail account, and the years it appears.
rows.caution: department and function code.

rows.grain: one row per abbreviated account name
rows.what_it_answers: A decoder, not data: what each ten-character MUNIS abbreviation expands to, and the basis for each expansion.
rows.caution: The expansions are ours except where `basis` says otherwise.

rows.grain: one row per table per annual report
rows.what_it_answers: A catalogue of what EXISTS, not of what has been extracted. Every table found by reading all sixteen annual reports end to end: its printed heading verbatim, its pages, its grain, its printed total, and whether it is extractable.
rows.caution: A catalogue of what EXISTS, not of what has been extracted.

rows.grain: one row per extracted table
rows.what_it_answers: What was actually READ: which tables, from which pages, how many figures, and whether the extract is checkable against a printed total.
rows.caution: from which pages

rows.grain: one row per revenue line per year
rows.what_it_answers: Town REVENUE — every receipt line the annual reports print, by name and amount, per year, FY2011–FY2023. Only five years are `checked` against the report's own printed total.
rows.caution: as printed.

rows.grain: one row per page surveyed
rows.what_it_answers: A measurement of PAGES, not of figures: per page, the extraction mode, how many gutters and money tokens it holds, how many characters and rows. This is how the right instrument is chosen per page.
rows.caution: A survey, not data: it measures pages, it does not read figures.

rows.grain: one row per fee per year
rows.what_it_answers: The published fee a family pays to play: dollars per fiscal year × school level × item, with the date it was set and the document that set it. Includes family caps and sibling discounts.
rows.caution: by level and year.

rows.grain: one row per sport per season per metric
rows.what_it_answers: Per sport × season × level: participation COUNTS and DOLLAR figures mixed in one table, told apart by `metric`. `raw` keeps the value exactly as printed and `is_numeric` says whether it parsed, because some cells are text.

rows.grain: one row per printed total
rows.what_it_answers: Not data — checks. For each total the source prints, what our rows sum to, the difference, and whether it ties.

rows.grain: one row per athletics figure per year
rows.what_it_answers: Athletics money from BOTH sides, and these are three different quantities that must never be added: what the town appropriated from the general fund, what the revolving fund took IN, and what the revolving fund SPENT. Dollars per year with the basis and source document for each.
rows.caution: Appropriation, fund revenue and fund spending are three quantities. Never add two of them.

rows.grain: one row per ballot question
rows.what_it_answers: VOTES, not dollars — though each carries the amount at stake. Per ballot question: type, purpose, yes / no / blank counts, registered voters, turnout and the result.

rows.grain: one row per line per year per stage per variant
rows.what_it_answers: Dollar amounts per budget LINE from the district's budget documents — no counts, no people. Each figure carries the stage it represents (proposed / settled / actual) and, for FY27, which of four whole budget scenarios it belongs to. FY2014–FY2027, 9,503 figures, plus a flag where two documents state different amounts for the same line-year.
rows.caution: Split on `stage` AND `variant`. FY27 carries four whole budgets.
rows.default_query: SELECT f.fy, f.stage, f.variant, f.label, f.value, b.section, b.function_group, f.doc_id FROM budget_figure f LEFT JOIN budget_line b USING (line_key) ORDER BY f.fy, f.stage, f.value DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per budget line
rows.what_it_answers: The district's LINE LIST — no money at all. One row per budget line with its section, its function group and what kind of line it is. This is the dimension `budget_figure` and `workbook_figure` hang their dollars on.
rows.caution: with its section and function group.

rows.grain: one row per year
rows.what_it_answers: Per year, how capital spending was PAID FOR: free cash, taxation, unexpended prior-year capital, other. Dollars.

rows.grain: one row per project
rows.what_it_answers: The FY27 capital plan as proposed: project, department, cost, running cumulative, whether it was funded and from where.
rows.caution: ranked.

rows.grain: one row per budget line mapped to an account
rows.what_it_answers: EMPTY, deliberately. It would map a budget line to a ledger account, and it cannot: MUNIS truncates names to ten characters so `MS GUIDANC` and `HS GUIDANC` collide. Only the CATEGORY joins, through `account.function`.
rows.caution: Deliberately empty. MUNIS truncates to ten characters so MS GUIDANC and HS GUIDANC collide; only the CATEGORY can be joined, through account.function. Populating this would record an inference as a mapping.
rows.default_query: SELECT * FROM crosswalk LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per dataset per document
rows.what_it_answers: The join between an extracted dataset and the document it came from: which pages, how many rows, whether it reconciled, and the publisher's own label, size and checksum.

rows.grain: one row per district per year per measure
rows.what_it_answers: The state's published measures for SEVEN districts -- Lunenburg and the six peers -- per year, SY2009-SY2025: enrollment, staffing FTE, per-pupil spending by function, demographics and MCAS. Each value carries whether it reconciles to DESE's own printed total.
rows.caution: SEVEN districts, not every one, despite what this row said until 8 September 2026 -- the RADAR workbook was scoped down so the published database would fit. `dese_function_statewide` is the all-district view. DESE dataset `er3w-dyti` publishes these same measures for all 421 districts and agrees with this table on all 2,982 values; percentages are stored here as 0.57 where DESE prints 57.0.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, district, measure, value, reconciles FROM dese_measure WHERE "group"='Expenditures Per Pupil' AND fy=2025 ORDER BY district, measure LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per year per measure
rows.what_it_answers: DESE's ALL-FUNDS per-pupil expenditure figures for every district. All funds means grants and revolving funds are included, so these are NOT comparable with a general fund appropriation.
rows.caution: All-funds, so NOT comparable with the town's general fund appropriation.

rows.grain: one row per source document
rows.what_it_answers: One row per source document: its archive path, how it reached us, its publisher URL, whether that link still opens (`link_state`), whether our copy still matches the publisher's (`copy_state`), and both checksums. Also which columns a workbook HIDES from a reader.
rows.caution: `link_state` says whether the publisher's copy still opens; `copy_state` whether it still matches ours.

rows.grain: one row per planned extract
rows.what_it_answers: What is planned to be read out of the annual reports and what state each item is in — including items deliberately not attempted, and why.
rows.caution: and what state each is in.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS period
rows.what_it_answers: What each MUNIS accounting period means and how many months of the year had elapsed. Period 13 is the year-end close after the lapse period, not a thirteenth month.
rows.caution: Period 13 is the year-end close after the lapse period, not a thirteenth month.

rows.grain: one row per line of the state's proof
rows.what_it_answers: The state's own line-by-line proof of certified free cash, for nine towns — every component with its role in the calculation. Dollars.
rows.caution: for nine towns.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS fund
rows.what_it_answers: One row per MUNIS fund: its number, its name, what kind of fund it is and what restricts it. No money.
rows.caution: with its kind and restriction.

rows.grain: one row per transaction
rows.what_it_answers: TRANSACTIONS — the athletics revolving fund line by line: effective and posting dates, journal, references, vendor, amount, running balance, check and warrant numbers, and the comments the clerk typed. The only transaction-level data in the archive, obtained by records request.
rows.caution: from a records request.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: Per fund per period: opening balance, revenue in, salaries, other expenditure, encumbered and closing balance. FY2026 period 9 only — and `opening_balance` is NULL for every one of the 61 funds.
rows.caution: spent and holds.
rows.default_query: SELECT a.fy, a.period, a.fund, f.name, f.kind, f.restriction, a.revenue, a.salaries, a.expenditure, a.encumbered, a.closing_balance FROM fund_activity a LEFT JOIN fund f USING (fund) ORDER BY a.closing_balance DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per grant per year
rows.what_it_answers: Grant AWARDS: name, amount in dollars, who holds it, and the fiscal year — except one ESSER award that genuinely spans FY21–24, which is why `fy` is TEXT here.
rows.caution: by name and amount.

rows.grain: one row per grant per year
rows.what_it_answers: The same awards with their source addresses and checksums, plus whether documents disagree about an amount and whether it is ESSER money.
rows.caution: `fy` is TEXT — see grant_award.

rows.grain: one row per account per year per period per document
rows.what_it_answers: BOTH revenue and expense accounts from the town's MUNIS books, told apart by `account_type` — revenue is stored NEGATIVE. Six money measures per row: original appropriation, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered, available, plus percent used. Two grains in the same table (`level`): 67 department roll-ups and 916 detail accounts. FY2026 only, at two periods — 9 carries the department rows, 12 the account rows.
rows.caution: at a moment in the year.
rows.default_query: SELECT l.fy, l.period, l.account_id, a.name, a.fund_name, a.dept, a.function, a.account_type, a.level, l.original, l.revised, l.expended, l.encumbered, l.available FROM ledger_snapshot l JOIN account a USING (account_id) ORDER BY l.fy, l.period, l.account_id LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per line per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Every budget line × year × stage as EXTRACTED, before disagreements between documents are resolved. Dollars. This is the raw reading; `budget_figure` is the settled one.
rows.caution: every year

rows.grain: one row per source document
rows.what_it_answers: Not figures — a report on extraction. Per source document: how many data rows, how many carried a usable layout, how many fell short of the expected column count, and why a document was or was not usable.

rows.grain: one row per disagreeing reading
rows.what_it_answers: One row per disagreeing READING: where two documents state different dollar amounts for the same line-year, both values are kept with their source and the spread between them. Nothing here is resolved.
rows.caution: Kept rather than resolved. Which document is right is often not established.

rows.grain: one row per budget book line
rows.what_it_answers: The district's budget book in ITS OWN shape: one row per line with every year's column side by side (FY23 actual through the four FY27 scenarios) rather than unpivoted. Includes the workbook's own comments column, which is where the district explains a line to itself.
rows.caution: in its own shape and column order.

rows.grain: one row per assumption
rows.what_it_answers: Every assumption the money model rests on, what it rests on, and what single document would settle it.
rows.caution: with what would settle it.

rows.grain: one row per revenue account or fund or department
rows.what_it_answers: Our model, not measurement. One row per revenue account, fund or department: what we classified it as, HOW that was established, and WHY. 252 rows covering every money node in the school and town diagrams.
rows.caution: `how` and `why` carry the basis so a classification can be argued with.

rows.grain: one row per traced edge
rows.what_it_answers: Where a restricted fund's money is PERMITTED to go, with the statute or grant award that permits it. An edge is a presumption about purpose, never an observation of spending.
rows.caution: An edge is the statute or grant award — a PRESUMPTION about purpose, never an observation of spending.

rows.grain: one row per gap
rows.what_it_answers: The honest list of what CANNOT be answered — per side (money in, money out), what is missing and why the published documents do not close it.
rows.caution: This table is the honest list of what cannot be answered.

rows.grain: one row per account per report
rows.what_it_answers: The MUNIS chart of accounts exactly as DELIVERED, before our normalisation — including the report parameters (`totals_only`, `suppress_zero`) that decide what a report shows and therefore what is missing from it.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Out-of-district special education tuition in DOLLARS, split private vs collaborative, per year per stage. Not a count of children — `placement_counts` is that, and the two do not divide into each other.
rows.caution: private and collaborative.

rows.grain: one row per year
rows.what_it_answers: CHILDREN, not dollars. Students placed outside the district, split collaborative / day / residential, measured on 1 March each year from SIMS Report 7. FY2013–FY2025. Carries its own checks: whether the parts sum to the total, and whether each year agrees with the next year's restatement of it.
rows.caution: split collaborative/day/residential.

rows.grain: one row per rate
rows.what_it_answers: Every rate and fee the model uses: the value, what kind of value it is, when it was set, when it expires, its source document and cell reference, and whether the model actually uses it.
rows.caution: with where it was set.

rows.grain: one row per anomaly
rows.what_it_answers: Things found while reading the annual reports that need a person: a total that does not tie, a heading that moved, a column that vanished.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: APPROPRIATIONS as the annual reports print them — the largest extract here, 4,665 rows across sixteen years. Values sit in ORDINAL columns (v1..v8) whose meaning changes page to page; `column_meaning` names them where the table states an identity that fixes them, and says `not established` where it does not.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Read `column_meaning` and split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Capital project funds as the annual reports print them: appropriated, expended, encumbered and balance, per article.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Outstanding DEBT and repayment schedules as the annual reports print them. Dollars, town-wide — school building debt is inside these figures and is not separated out.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Departmental activity tables — permits issued, inspections done, cases handled. Mostly COUNTS rather than dollars, and what is counted differs by department and by year.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Election results as the annual reports print them: candidates, offices and vote counts in ordinal columns.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Enrollment counts and MCAS results as the annual reports print them. Mixed measures in ordinal columns; read `column_meaning` before using any of them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: GROSS WAGES paid per named employee per year, as the annual reports print them. 3,545 rows. Actual pay rather than budget, including overtime and details.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Figures for Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School as the annual reports print them. A DIFFERENT DISTRICT: Lunenburg pays it an assessment, and its figures must never be added to Lunenburg's own schools.
rows.caution: Monty Tech is a DIFFERENT DISTRICT. Never add it to Lunenburg's schools.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Names and offices of town officials as each annual report lists them. No money.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Trust fund balances and activity as the annual reports print them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Assessed property VALUATION by class, as the annual reports print it. Dollars — and the base the tax levy is computed on.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Counts of births, marriages and deaths as the annual reports print them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per revenue source per year
rows.what_it_answers: The checked subset of the above joined to our classification: the printed name, our normalised key, what KIND of revenue it is (levy, state aid, local receipt, transfer, one-time), the amount, and the document and page it came from. Five years.
rows.caution: with our classification of what KIND it is.

rows.grain: one row per printed roster title
rows.what_it_answers: Our classification of each printed roster title into a role category and grade, with how it was classified. Judgement, recorded so it can be disputed.

rows.grain: one row per school fund
rows.what_it_answers: The schools' own funds at one moment (FY26 period 9): per fund, revenue received, salaries paid, other expenditure, encumbered, and the balance left. Dollars.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year
rows.what_it_answers: Every fund OUTSIDE the general appropriation, FY2011–FY2025: balance brought forward, receipts, disbursements, balance carried forward. Grants, revolving funds and gifts that pay for real staff and appear nowhere in the appropriation. Dollars.
rows.caution: fifteen years

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education paraprofessionals, split by school, per year per stage. A budget line, never a headcount.
rows.caution: A budget line, not a headcount.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education teachers, split by school, per year per stage. A budget line, never a headcount.
rows.caution: A budget line, not a headcount.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education transportation, per year per stage.

rows.grain: one row per printed roster title
rows.what_it_answers: A lookup, not data: each printed roster title, how many times it was seen, and the position it maps to.

rows.grain: one row per school per position per year
rows.what_it_answers: Counts of the names above, per school × position × year. A count of names the town printed. It is not a staffing level and cannot be turned into one.
rows.caution: A count of NAMES, with no FTE and no funding source. It is not a staffing level.

rows.grain: one row per person per year
rows.what_it_answers: PEOPLE — one row per name the town printed, per year, with the school, the page, the printed job title and our classification of it. FY2011–FY2025, 3,815 entries. No FTE, no salary, no funding source, and undated within the year.
rows.caution: name by name

rows.grain: one row per figure the town stated
rows.what_it_answers: Figures the town or district ASSERTED in their own words, with the quote, who said it, when, and what it supersedes. Claims, kept as claims.
rows.caution: with the quote.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: One dollar total per year per stage — the district's own stated total expenses, as each document states it.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: One dollar total per year per stage — the district's own stated total salaries.

rows.grain: one row per department
rows.what_it_answers: The town's 67 departments at FY26 period 9: appropriation, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered, available and percent used. EXPENSE side only, department grain only.
rows.caution: by department.

rows.grain: one row per function group
rows.what_it_answers: Computed, not read: per function group, how far spending ran from budget across years — budgeted, spent, net, gross, churn, and the best and worst years.
rows.caution: across years.

rows.grain: one row per worksheet row per year per column
rows.what_it_answers: The FY27 budget workbook unpivoted to one row per worksheet row × year × column, so every figure is quotable by its spreadsheet coordinate. `column_kind` says which printed column — final_budget, actual_to_date, encumbered_to_date. Dollars only.
rows.caution: every cell quotable by its row.
rows.default_query: SELECT w.fy, w.column_kind, w.row_kind, w.row, b.label, w.value FROM workbook_figure w LEFT JOIN budget_line b USING (line_key) ORDER BY w.fy, w.row LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per table in this database
rows.what_it_answers: This page's own source. One row per table: its role, whose money it is, how finely it resolves money, its grain, what it holds, and what goes wrong if it is used carelessly.
rows.caution: Self-describing, and checked both ways: a table with no row here fails the build, and a row naming a table that no longer exists fails it too.

rows.grain: one row per DISTINCT column name across the whole database
rows.what_it_answers: One row per DISTINCT column name across the whole database: what it means, its unit, whether it is published or ours, and the caution attached to it.
rows.caution: Keyed on the NAME, not on table plus name, because `v1` and `status` mean the same dangerous thing everywhere they appear. Where a name genuinely differs by table, the table entry says so.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year
rows.what_it_answers: The special revenue schedule READ from the rendered page rather than OCR'd: balance brought forward, total receipts, total disbursements, balance carried forward, per fund. **The only version of this table that ties to its own printed grand total** — FY2022, 167 funds, all four columns to the penny and every row balancing.
rows.caution: A figure read off an image is a READING, not a published number — same status as the OCR's. It is trustworthy because the report's own printed total and the table's own identity both check it, not because a model produced it. Years that do not tie are not in here.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, page, [group], fund, forward, receipts, disbursements, carried, row_ties FROM special_revenue_read ORDER BY fy, page, rowid LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per edition
rows.what_it_answers: The GRAND TOTAL each annual report PRINTS for the special revenue schedule, quoted with its page. Four columns.
rows.caution: This is the independent check on `special_revenue_read`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows — the OCR misread this very figure by $1,010 and the reconciliation was measured against it for months.

rows.grain: one row per line per fund column per year
rows.what_it_answers: What the town HOLDS, read from the COMBINED BALANCE SHEET — assets, liabilities and fund equity across six fund columns (general, special revenue, enterprise, capital project, trust and agency, long-term debt). Everything else in this archive measures money MOVING; this is the only table that measures what is sitting there.
rows.caution: Read from the page, like `special_revenue_read`. It is trusted because three checks hold: each column foots to its own printed total, the sheet's identity (liabilities + fund equity = assets) holds per column, and special revenue + enterprise fund equity ties to the special revenue schedule's carried-forward total — an INDEPENDENT document. One printed sheet does not balance itself (FY2019 trust and agency, $657,297.35 apart); that is the town's print, recorded not corrected.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, section, line, fund, amount FROM balance_sheet ORDER BY fy, section, line LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per printed total per fund column per year
rows.what_it_answers: The totals each balance sheet PRINTS — total assets, total liabilities, total fund equity — quoted with the page they appear on.
rows.caution: The independent check on `balance_sheet`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows.

rows.grain: one row per line per fund column per printing per year
rows.what_it_answers: What the four ENTERPRISE funds hold at 30 June — Sewer, Water, Solid Waste and PEG Access, side by side, with a memorandum-only total column. Read from the COMBINING BALANCE SHEET — ENTERPRISE FUNDS, which is the only balance sheet FY2024 and FY2025 print; neither report contains the town-wide combined balance sheet `balance_sheet` holds for FY2011–FY2023.
rows.caution: RATEPAYER MONEY. Sewer and water user charges, betterments, trash fees and cable franchise money — none of it is available to the town's general operations and none of it is a tax dollar. This is NOT an extension of `balance_sheet`: that table's `enterprise` value is one of six fund-type COLUMNS on a different sheet, and the two must never be unioned. FY2024 prints the same sheet TWICE (printed pages 21 and 28), so `printing` is 1 or 2 and must be collapsed on before anything is summed — summing across it doubles the money. FY2024's memorandum column is $102,000.00 out on two offsetting lines; that is the town's print, recorded not corrected. Only cells that print a figure are recorded; the sheet's 0.00 and '-' template cells are not rows here.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, section, line, fund, amount FROM enterprise_balance_sheet WHERE printing = 1 ORDER BY fy, section, line LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per printed total per fund column per printing per year
rows.what_it_answers: The totals the enterprise balance sheet PRINTS — Total Assets, Total Liabilities, Total Fund Equity, Total Liabilities and Fund Equity, and the sheet's own PROOF row — quoted with the raw cell text and the page.
rows.caution: The independent check on `enterprise_balance_sheet`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows. The PROOF row is the sheet's own self-check and is what a reading is reconciled to. FY2025 prints its Proof as '(0.00)' and '-' in different columns; the amount recorded is 0.00 and the raw glyph is in `quote`.

rows.grain: one row per printed expense line per year
rows.what_it_answers: What the town's PEG Access / Public Access Cable operation spent, line by line, FY2015-FY2025, read from the expense table each annual town report prints. From FY2020 the report also prints a `% of Expense` column and it is recorded here beside the amount.
rows.caution: CABLE FRANCHISE MONEY, not tax money. Comcast pays it under the Town's cable licence; from FY2020 it sits in a PEG Access enterprise fund established under MGL c.44 s53F1/2 and is appropriated by its own Town Meeting article. None of it is available to general operations. The line LIST changes: `Insurance` disappears after FY2020 and `Indirect Costs` appears, so a line-by-line series across that boundary is comparing different things. FY2017's ten lines add to 450.01 MORE than that report's own printed TOTAL; the total is what the rest of the record uses. Join to `peg_access_printed_totals` for the total each year actually prints -- never sum these rows and call it the year's expenses without saying so.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, line, amount, pct FROM peg_access ORDER BY fy, ordinal LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per printed figure per statement per year
rows.what_it_answers: The REVENUE vs EXPENSES statement each report prints, row by row in printed order, plus the line-item TOTAL and what the prose says the revenue was -- each with the raw cell text, the printed page and the PDF index.
rows.caution: `total_row` is the label the page prints and it is NOT unique: FY2019's statement carries two rows labelled `Subtotal`. Use `ordinal`. The rows do not mean the same thing across years -- FY2015-FY2019 `Starting Balance` is the prior year's Ending Balance, FY2021 and FY2025 it is the BUDGET, and FY2022 has no balance at all, so `TOTAL` there is one year's surplus and not a fund balance. `precision` says whether the statement is printed in cents or whole dollars; FY2024 and FY2025 are in dollars while the expense table beside them is in cents.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, ordinal, total_row, amount, precision FROM peg_access_printed_totals WHERE statement = 'revenue_vs_expenses' ORDER BY fy, ordinal LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per arithmetic statement each PEG statement makes about itself
rows.what_it_answers: The arithmetic the printed statement states about itself, written over the row ORDINALS in `peg_access_printed_totals` -- `1 + 2 = 3` and so on. It is transcribed from the page, because the arithmetic changes every few years.
rows.caution: This is what `verify_peg_access.py` recomputes, and it is also a completeness check: every printed row must be reached by some identity. FY2020's row 5 is not, and that is recorded as a printed defect rather than removed.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, identity, note FROM peg_access_identities ORDER BY fy, identity LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per year per function code per level
rows.what_it_answers: DESE's spending by function code with the GENERAL FUND and GRANTS/REVOLVING money in separate columns, SY2009-SY2025, for Lunenburg and its six peers. The only published split of the two in this archive: Lunenburg SY2025 shows $478,097 of grant and revolving money against function 2330, Paraprofessionals, beside $1,338,477 of general fund.
rows.caution: Filter on `level` before aggregating ANYTHING. The source puts rollups beside detail and nothing in its column names says which is which -- summing every Lunenburg SY2025 row gives $117,996,913 against an in-district total of $27,903,187. level='total' is TTPP; level='rollup' is IIII and OODD; level='category' is the ten in-district categories plus ODTR and COMM; level='detail' is the printed function codes, plus TUIT, which has no category row. ODTR is already inside OODD -- adding it again double counts -- and its detail is only ever code 9130, a component and not the whole, which is what `reconciles='partial'` means. This is DESE's definition of spending, all funds, and it is NOT the town's appropriation; it must never be subtracted from one. A function code is not a budget line and not a post, so this bounds the funding-source question rather than settling it.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, district, func_cat_code, func_desc, gen_fund, grants_revolving, total, per_pupil, reconciles FROM dese_function_expenditure WHERE level='category' AND lea='01620000' AND fy >= 2021 ORDER BY fy DESC, total DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per year per function code per level, across every Massachusetts district
rows.what_it_answers: Where Lunenburg sits among all Massachusetts districts on per-pupil spending, function by function, SY2009-SY2025 -- min, quartiles, median, max, Lunenburg's own figure and its rank. Also the statewide dollar totals and the share of each function paid by grants and revolving money rather than the general fund.
rows.caution: Read the denominator before quoting a rank. `districts` is the denominator and it INCLUDES charter and virtual districts, which are in DESE's file and are not municipal school districts. `per_pupil_basis` says on every row whether a per-pupil figure exists at all: DESE prints 0 against every out-of-district row, so the quartiles are blank there rather than a median of zeros. Filter on `level` here too -- a category and its own detail are separate rows.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, func_cat_code, func_desc, districts, per_pupil_median, lunenburg_per_pupil, lunenburg_rank_of_districts, grant_share FROM dese_function_statewide WHERE level='category' AND fy=2025 ORDER BY per_pupil_median DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per organisation per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Teacher FTE split into general education, special education, career/technical and English learner, per state, district and school, SY2008-SY2026, for Lunenburg and its six peers. This is where Lunenburg's special education teacher FTE falls from 18.5 to 2.0 while its total FTE holds flat.
rows.caution: Filter `org_level` before summing ANYTHING: state, district and school rows sit in one table. A DISTRICT ROW IS NOT THE SUM OF ITS SCHOOL ROWS -- staff with no school assignment have a district row and no school row, and the gap reaches several hundred FTE in the largest districts, so the two must not be added or differenced. FTE here is EPIMS FTE, defined per ASSIGNMENT rather than per person, so it is not comparable with a budget line that pays whole salaries. The sped collapse is the signature of RECODING; nothing here establishes that staff left.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, org_name, org_level, gen_ed_fte, sped_fte, career_tech_fte, el_fte, total_fte, reconciles FROM dese_teacher_program_area WHERE lea='01620000' AND org_level='district' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per organisation per subject per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Teacher FTE by subject, with the share licensed, the share teaching in field, the share experienced and the students-per-teacher ratio, SY2008-SY2026.
rows.caution: `teacher_fte` IS AN FTE even though DESE names the column `TCHR_CNT`. Filter `subject_level`: `all` is every teacher, `group` is `Core-All Subjects` and `Total Non-Core Academic Subjects` which are groups of the subjects beside them, and the members therefore DO NOT PARTITION -- summing subjects double counts. `students_per_teacher` is parsed from the sentence DESE prints, which is kept beside it in `student_teacher_ratio_printed`. A SUBJECT ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE for an organisation and year we hold is a PUBLISHED ZERO, not a gap: rows with no FTE at all are not written, and they outnumber the real ones.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, subject, subject_level, teacher_fte, licensed_pct, in_field_pct, student_teacher_ratio_printed FROM dese_teacher_subject WHERE lea='01620000' AND org_level='district' AND fy=2026 ORDER BY teacher_fte DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per organisation per subject per school year, FTE split across six grade bands
rows.what_it_answers: Teacher FTE by grade band AND subject AND school. This breaks a limit recorded here as structural: the town's staff rosters give grade detail with no FTE, and DESE elsewhere gives FTE with no grade. This gives both.
rows.caution: Two level columns and both matter: `org_level` and `subject_level`. Summing every subject for one organisation counts each teacher about three times over -- the build asserts that it would, so a lost level column fails there rather than in your query. `agrees_with_teacher_subject` is written on the `All` rows only and says whether this dataset and `dese_teacher_subject` state the same total FTE for that organisation; where they do not, BOTH are kept and neither corrects the other. A SUBJECT ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE for an organisation and year we hold is a PUBLISHED ZERO, not a gap -- rows where every grade band and the total are nought are not written, and they outnumber the real rows two to one. That is the opposite of the usual reading here, which is why it is said twice. `printing` is part of the key: DESE publishes the same organisation, subject and year twice with different figures in a small number of cases, and both are kept.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, subject, pk_2_fte, grade_3_5_fte, grade_6_8_fte, grade_9_12_fte, multi_grade_fte, total_fte, reconciles FROM dese_teacher_grade_subject WHERE lea='01620000' AND org_level='district' AND fy=2026 AND total_fte > 0 ORDER BY total_fte DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per race/ethnicity per job class per school year
rows.what_it_answers: HEADCOUNT by job class -- Administrator, Teacher, Paraprofessional, Other Licensed, Other Non-Licensed -- with hires and retention, SY2021-SY2023. The only DESE table here that counts administrators and paraprofessionals as PEOPLE rather than as FTE or as dollars.
rows.caution: `race_level` is the level column and getting it wrong doubles every figure. `All Educators` is a TOTAL row sitting beside the seven reported races; summing the whole job class gives exactly twice the truth, and this project's own notes recorded 118 paraprofessionals and 38 administrators for SY2023 that way when the file holds 59 and 19. There is no all-job-classes row, so a district total is the sum of the five `race_level='all'` rows and no published figure states it. Headcount is not FTE: a half-time director and a principal are one each. Three years is a thin series on a base of tens, and a reclassification would look identical to a change in staffing.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, job_class, educators_headcount, hires_headcount, retained_headcount, retained_pct FROM dese_educator_workforce WHERE lea='01620000' AND race_level='all' ORDER BY fy DESC, educators_headcount DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per organisation per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Enrollment by grade and by selected population -- English learner, low income, economically disadvantaged, high needs, students with disabilities -- per state, district and school, back to SY1992. The denominator for nearly every rate on this site.
rows.caution: Filter `org_level`. `swd_cnt` is a published count of students with disabilities and it agrees exactly with `dese_sped_program` for Lunenburg SY2026; it does NOT agree with the denominator the staffing ratios in `dese_sped_indicator` use, which is twelve lower in the same year. A per-pupil figure is a division by a count whose definition has to be stated with it -- DESE publishes at least four different counts of Lunenburg's children and none of them equal, see money_gaps.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, org_name, org_level, total_cnt, swd_cnt, swd_pct, econ_disadvantaged_pct, el_cnt FROM dese_enrollment WHERE lea='01620000' AND fy >= 2020 ORDER BY fy DESC, org_level, org_name LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per grade group per student group per indicator per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Special education indicators SY2017-SY2026: the context counts, the special education staffing ratios per 100 students with disabilities, and the outcome, assessment and postsecondary measures, each with students with disabilities set beside students without.
rows.caution: Three things. (1) `grades_level` says `all` or `subset` and THE SUBSETS OVERLAP -- Grade 10 is inside Grades 9-12 is inside K-12 -- so no sum across `grades` means anything. (2) `denominator_cnt` is the population the percentage is OF; the indicator's own figure is `measure_cnt`, and on the SPECIAL EDUCATION STAFF rows `measure_cnt` is the students-with-disabilities denominator while `measure_pct` is the FTE per 100 of them. (3) `value_type` says whether a row is a percentage, an average, an FTE or an FTE per 100 -- read it before doing arithmetic. The staffing ratios times the count are what produce the unresolved $69,161 per paraprofessional FTE; see money_gaps. `printing` is part of the key -- DESE publishes a handful of these rows twice -- so collapse on it before aggregating.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, grades, student_group, indicator, measure_cnt, measure_pct, value_type FROM dese_sped_indicator WHERE lea='01620000' AND indicator_category='SPECIAL EDUCATION STAFF' ORDER BY fy DESC, indicator LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per indicator category per indicator per school year
rows.what_it_answers: What the students with disabilities are: disability type, race, gender, grade span, in district against out of district, placement, and the special education FTE ratios. SY2020-SY2026. It carries a PUBLISHED count of students with disabilities, which used to be reachable here only by multiplying a percentage by enrollment.
rows.caution: `indicator_level` is `total` or `member` and every category carries its own total row. Three categories do not behave like the others: `Placement` runs SHORT of its own total because its four members are IN-DISTRICT placements and children placed out of district appear in the total and in none of them; `Disability Type` is a collapsed rendering of `Disability Type All` with several disabilities folded into `Other Disability`, so adding the two counts every child twice; and `Special Education FTEs per 100 SWDs` is a RATIO despite sitting in the same column and despite `value_type` saying `Percent` on every row of this file. `printing` is part of the key: 95 rows are published twice, most of them the same district under two different names (`Ayer Shirley` and `Ayer Shirley School District` share one org code). Collapse on it before aggregating.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, indicator_category, indicator, indicator_level, measure_cnt, measure_pct FROM dese_sped_program WHERE lea='01620000' AND fy=2026 AND indicator_category='Disability Type All' ORDER BY measure_cnt DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per grade span per starting placement per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Where a child's placement started and where the same children are now -- no IEP, included, substantially separate, or out of district. SY2018-SY2026. Out-of-district tuition is the largest single line in the special education budget and this is the pathway into it.
rows.caution: THE BASES ARE TINY. A Lunenburg cohort is tens of children, so a percentage here must never travel without its count -- 14.3% of 28 is four children, and one year of one cohort establishes nothing. `grade_span` K-12 and K-2 OVERLAP and must never be summed. `unaccounted_cnt` is the cohort less the four destinations: what it IS -- moved away, left for a private school, aged out, suppressed -- is not established by this file.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, grade_span, placement_at_start, cohort_cnt, no_iep_cnt, included_cnt, sub_separate_cnt, out_of_district_cnt, unaccounted_cnt FROM dese_sped_trajectory WHERE lea='01620000' ORDER BY fy DESC, grade_span, placement_at_start LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per grade group per school year
rows.what_it_answers: Caseload movement: how many children entered special education services in a year and how many left. The dynamic behind the spending line that a headcount alone cannot show. SY2019-SY2025.
rows.caution: TWO TRAPS. `repeats_prior_year` is `yes` where all four figures exactly equal the same district's previous year -- Lunenburg's SY2024 and SY2025 are such a pair, and four independently counted quantities landing identically two years running is not plausible where a row carried forward is. Never sum two such years as two years of movement. And `grade_rows_sum` is NOT `enrolled_cnt`: the grade rows are not the K-12 row broken down, because the `Grade 12` row is a fraction of the size of the others. What the residual is has not been established.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, grades, enrolled_cnt, on_iep_cnt, moved_in_cnt, moved_out_cnt, moved_in_cnt - moved_out_cnt AS net, repeats_prior_year FROM dese_sped_movement WHERE lea='01620000' AND grades_level='all' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per school year per town of residence per enrollment reason per enrolling district
rows.what_it_answers: Where a town's resident children actually go to school, and who arrives from where, SY2014-SY2026, by reason: school choice, charter, tuitioned in several ways, METCO, foster care. Both directions of the choice question, and the headcounts behind the choice dollars on the cherry sheet.
rows.caution: ONE TABLE FROM TWO DATASET IDS. DESE publishes `vxt3-k35x` as Sending and `8xyg-59b2` as Receiving; compared row by row they hold the IDENTICAL rows and differ only in column order, so they are one measurement published twice and are loaded once. Do not treat a net position drawn from this as resting on two agreeing sources. Filter on `town` for children leaving, on `lea` for children arriving; `town='Lunenburg' AND lea='01620000'` is the resident children who stay. SCOPED: every row about Lunenburg in either direction plus both directions for the six peers, because 74,878 statewide rows would take the published database past Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. The two source files were compared on all 74,878 rows before scoping, so the claim that they are one dataset published twice covers the whole publication.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, enrollment_reason, district, students FROM dese_town_enrollment WHERE town='Lunenburg' AND fy=2026 AND lea <> '01620000' ORDER BY students DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per fiscal year
rows.what_it_answers: The Chapter 70 formula term by term for every Massachusetts district, FY1993-FY2026: foundation enrollment, foundation budget, required local contribution, aid, required net school spending and what was actually spent. Thirty-four years. It answers a question nobody in town can currently put a number on -- does Lunenburg spend above or below the minimum the state requires -- and its FY2026 aid figure ties exactly to the town's own MUNIS revenue ledger.
rows.caution: THREE COLUMN NAMES IN THE SOURCE MEAN TWO THINGS EACH. `required_nss` is the workbook's column I, the formula's own arithmetic; `required_nss_published` is column J, what DESE publishes with carryover included, and the two differ in over a thousand district-years. `ch70_aid` and `ch70_aid_after_penalties` are columns H and M. AND `nss_stage` IS LOAD-BEARING: the source column is headed `actualNSS` for all thirty-four years, but FY2025 and FY2026 hold BUDGETED net school spending. Rule 1 -- a rate measured from an actual to a budget is partly growth and partly the step between the two. Publish the ratio to required as a measurement and never as a verdict: the required minimum is a floor, not a standard of adequacy. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and `dese_ch70_statewide` keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, foundation_enrollment, foundation_budget, required_local_contribution, ch70_aid, required_nss_published, net_school_spending, nss_stage, nss_pct_of_required FROM dese_ch70_formula WHERE lea='01620000' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per fiscal year
rows.what_it_answers: The aid build-up, term by term, FY2007 on: every increment the Chapter 70 formula adds between the foundation budget and the aid actually paid, and every reduction it applies. This is what lets anybody model how the aid RESPONDS to a change in enrollment rather than assuming it moves linearly.
rows.caution: `level` separates the state row from the districts. Its `ch70_aid` agrees with `dese_ch70_formula` in every district-year they share, checked on every build -- they are two sheets of one workbook, not two sources. The increments are the formula's own machinery and several are zero in most years by design; a zero here is a term that did not apply, not a missing figure. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and `dese_ch70_statewide` keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, foundation_enrollment, foundation_budget, target_aid_pct, foundation_aid_increment, minimum_aid_increment, ch70_aid FROM dese_ch70_aid_factor WHERE lea='01620000' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per MUNICIPALITY per fiscal year
rows.what_it_answers: The municipal side of the Chapter 70 formula: equalized valuation, income, the effort each implies, the target local contribution and how the required contribution was arrived at. This is where the town's ability to pay is computed, and it is the half of the formula the school budget never shows.
rows.caution: A DIFFERENT GRAIN FROM EVERY OTHER CHAPTER 70 TABLE HERE: a row is a TOWN, not a district, and `lea_number` is the workbook's own municipal key rather than a DESE org code. For a regional district several towns contribute to one district, so this must not be joined one to one with `dese_ch70_formula`. AND THE TOWN'S REQUIRED CONTRIBUTION IS NOT THE DISTRICT'S: for FY2026 Lunenburg the town figure is $14,605,342 and the Lunenburg school district figure in `dese_ch70_formula` is $13,334,631, because a town also contributes to any regional district it belongs to. Every district is kept here rather than the seven-district peer scope the other Chapter 70 tables use, because a town in a regional district has a contribution row and no district row and scoping by district would drop exactly those.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, municipality, equalized_valuation, income, combined_effort_yield, target_local_contribution, required_local_contribution FROM dese_ch70_contribution WHERE municipality LIKE 'Lunenburg%' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per district per FISCAL year
rows.what_it_answers: State reimbursement for high-cost special education placements, FY2006-FY2026, split into instruction and tuition against transportation, with prior-year adjustments and relief payments separated -- so a year's receipt can be told apart from a year's entitlement. It also carries `eligible_students_claimed`, a count of CHILDREN.
rows.caution: **KEYED ON FISCAL YEAR, NOT SCHOOL YEAR.** Every other DESE table here is school year, and this repository has already had a fiscal-year type error that matched nothing silently. This is money the district RECEIVES and it does not appear in the general fund appropriation the town votes -- rule 11: a budget line that fell because circuit breaker rose is not a line that got cheaper. `eligible_students_claimed` counts CLAIMS, which is not the same set as the children in `sources/data/placement-counts.csv`. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and `dese_ch70_statewide` keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, eligible_students_claimed, total_eligible_expenses, total_net_claim, total_quarterly_payment, prior_year_adjustment FROM dese_circuit_breaker WHERE lea='01620000' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per fiscal year per measure, across every Massachusetts district
rows.what_it_answers: Where Lunenburg sits among every Massachusetts district on four ratios: net school spending as a share of what the state requires, Chapter 70 aid per foundation pupil, the required local contribution as a share of the foundation budget, and circuit breaker claim per eligible student. Min, quartiles, median, max, Lunenburg's own figure and its rank.
rows.caution: Read the denominator before quoting a rank -- `districts` is it, and it counts only districts that reported the measure that year. `basis` says on every row what the ratio is OF, because each is a division by a count or a dollar whose definition has to travel with it: foundation enrollment is not a headcount of children in the buildings, and the circuit breaker rows are FISCAL year where the rest are the Chapter 70 fiscal year. Publish the share-of-required as a measurement and never as a verdict -- the required minimum is a floor, not a standard of adequacy, and a district above it is not thereby adequately funded.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, measure, districts, p25, median, p75, lunenburg, lunenburg_rank_of_districts FROM dese_ch70_statewide WHERE measure='net school spending as a share of required' ORDER BY fy DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per reduction or restoration NAMED in a district budget document
rows.what_it_answers: What the district said in writing it was cutting, cycle by cycle, FY2020 to FY2027 — the position, the school, the FTE and the dollar figure WHERE THE DOCUMENT PRINTS THEM, and the district’s own stated consequence, quoted. Every row is a CLAIM: a reduction list is a document somebody assembled to argue for a budget (rule 13a), so `basis` is `stated` on all 193 rows and none of it is evidence that a post was removed. `direction` separates a reduction from a restoration or an addition; `conditional_on` records that FY2025 has TWO lists, one for each outcome of a ballot question that passed. /cut-register sets DESE’s teacher counts beside it.
rows.caution: NEVER aggregate across documents without splitting on `doc_date`: a position named on three lists in one cycle is three rows, because the register keeps every draft. Most rows carry no FTE and no amount because the document printed none, and a blank is an absence in the SOURCE rather than in the extract.

rows.grain: one row per organisation per subject per school year
rows.what_it_answers: HOW MANY CLASSES RAN, and how full they were, by school and by subject, SY2011-SY2025. The only table here that counts what was TAUGHT rather than who was employed, what was appropriated or how many children enrolled -- so it is what answers "did the cuts change what a child can take" without reaching for teacher FTE, which cannot tell four Spanish sections from two.
rows.caution: THREE SPLITS BEFORE ANY SUM. `org_type` separates the DISTRICT rollup from its own schools. `subj` = "All" is a rollup of the 25 named subjects beside it. And the fifteen subjects prefixed "CH74 - " are a SECOND, PARALLEL classification -- Chapter 74 vocational programme areas, every Lunenburg row of them zero -- which are not part of the subject total. THE THREE FIGURE COLUMNS ARE THREE QUANTITIES: `tot_clss_cnt` is classes that ran, `avg_clss_cnt` is DESE’s own average class size (seats over classes), and `tot_stu_cnt` is DISTINCT students who took the subject -- NOT seats, and not the product of the other two. `sy` is the school year ENDING and equals `fy` in every other DESE table here; it keeps the publisher’s own column name. AND A SCHOOL NAME IS NOT A FIXED SCHOOL: Lunenburg High held grades 8-12 from SY2013 to SY2016 and grades 9-12 either side, so join `dese_enrollment` for the grade span before comparing two years. The demographic percentage columns OVERLAP each other and may never be added. Two school-years report an average class size no primary school can have -- 87.1 in SY2011 and 36.5 in SY2022, both Lunenburg Primary -- so the elementary series is not trendable.
rows.default_query: SELECT sy, org_name, subj, tot_clss_cnt, avg_clss_cnt, tot_stu_cnt FROM dese_class_size WHERE org_name='Lunenburg High' AND sy=2025 AND tot_clss_cnt > 0 ORDER BY tot_clss_cnt DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per account per year at period 13
rows.what_it_answers: What was appropriated against what was actually spent, at the year-end close: original appropriation, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered and what was left over (`surplus`), with the leftover as a percent of the revised budget. Over `ledger_snapshot` joined to `account`, filtered to `period = 13`.
rows.caution: EMPTY TODAY -- it returns 0 rows. `ledger_snapshot` holds FY2026 at periods 9 and 12 only, and period 13 (the year-end close after the lapse period, per `fiscal_period`) has not been obtained. Nothing in the view says so; an empty result here is a document we do not hold, not a town that appropriated nothing. It also does not filter `account_type`, so when period 13 arrives revenue accounts -- stored NEGATIVE in `ledger_snapshot` -- will appear beside expense ones and `surplus_pct` on them will not mean what it means on an expense line. Two grains sit together: filter `level` before summing.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, fund, dept, name, level, original, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered, surplus, surplus_pct FROM v_appropriation_vs_spend ORDER BY surplus DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per disagreeing reading (line, year, stage, variant, source document)
rows.what_it_answers: Where two documents state DIFFERENT dollar amounts for the same budget line and year -- both readings kept, each with the document it came from and the `spread` between them. This is the table to read when you want to know which budget figures are disputed and by how much, and which document said what. A pass-through of `line_history_disagreements` with the numbers cast to REAL.
rows.caution: Nothing here is resolved: which document is right is usually not established, and `is_kept` records which reading the model took, not which is correct. Rows are READINGS, not lines -- counting rows counts documents, so use COUNT(DISTINCT line_key || fy) for a count of disputed line-years. Split on `stage` and `variant`: 254 of the disagreeing line-year-stage cells are at stage `proposed` and only 45 `settled` and 35 `restated`, so a disagreement is most often two proposals, not a contested actual.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, stage, line_key, label, source, value, is_kept, spread, kind FROM v_budget_disagreement ORDER BY spread DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per line per year per stage per named scenario
rows.what_it_answers: The FY27 budget SCENARIOS side by side -- the four whole budgets the district published (Balanced, Core Budget, Level Service, Restoration), 250 lines each. Every row of `budget_figure` whose `variant` is not blank, which is exactly the figures that belong to a named scenario rather than to the year.
rows.caution: These are FOUR ALTERNATIVE BUDGETS for the same year, not four parts of one. Summing across `variant` counts the same year four times; always group by `variant`. None of them is the year's budget -- the un-scenarioed figures are the ones with `variant = ''`, which this view deliberately excludes. A scenario is a proposal, never something that happened.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, variant, stage, label, value, doc_id FROM v_budget_scenario ORDER BY variant, value DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per account per year per non-final period
rows.what_it_answers: Spending PACE part-way through the year: how much of the revised budget has been expended, how much is expended-plus-encumbered, and `pace_gap` -- the committed share minus the share of the year elapsed. A positive `pace_gap` is a line committed ahead of the calendar. Over `ledger_snapshot` at every period `fiscal_period` marks not final.
rows.caution: IT DOES NOT FILTER `account_type`, so 224 of its 983 rows are REVENUE accounts, whose amounts are stored negative -- `spent_share` on those is not a burn rate at all (PS TUITION reads 7.53). Filter `a.account_type = 'expense'` yourself, which means joining `account` again. `pace_gap` is a calendar proxy, not a schedule: it assumes even spending across twelve months, and nothing here establishes that any line spends evenly. `fiscal_period` marks period 12 as not final, so period-12 rows carry `year_elapsed = 1.0`. Two grains: period 9 carries department roll-ups AND accounts, period 12 accounts only.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, dept, name, year_elapsed, spent_share, committed_share, pace_gap, available_now FROM v_burn WHERE period = 9 ORDER BY pace_gap DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per DESE function code per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: The town's ledger rolled up to DESE FUNCTION CODE -- revised, expended and encumbered summed per function, with a count of the accounts behind it and a count of the district budget lines whose `function_group` starts with the same four characters. The crosswalk between how the Town codes spending and how the district's book groups it.
rows.caution: `budget_lines` is a COUNT OF LINES, not dollars -- it is how many budget lines carry that function group, and it is 0 for 5 of the 46 function codes, which is a code the district's book does not use rather than a function nobody budgeted. Expense accounts only, and only accounts where `a.function` is set; anything uncoded is silently absent, so these sums do not add to the town's total. FY2026 period 12 only.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, function_code, accounts, budget_lines, ledger_revised, ledger_expended, ledger_encumbered FROM v_function_budget_vs_ledger ORDER BY ledger_expended DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per fund per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: Every town FUND on one line: what came in (`revenue`), what went out (`spent`, salaries plus other expenditure added together), and what the fund is holding at the end (`closing_balance`), with the fund's name, kind and what restricts it. This is where to look for money that is not the general fund -- revolving funds, grants, the circuit breaker, trusts.
rows.caution: `opening_balance` is not carried here and is NULL for all 61 funds in `fund_activity` anyway, so `closing_balance` cannot be reconciled to a starting point. FY2026 period 9 only -- a balance at 31 March, not a year end. `spent` FOLDS salaries and expenditure together; query `fund_activity` if you need them apart. The join to `fund` is a LEFT JOIN, so `name`, `kind` and `restriction` can be NULL for a fund the fund dimension does not carry.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, fund, name, kind, restriction, revenue, spent, closing_balance FROM v_fund_year ORDER BY closing_balance DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per interfund transfer-in revenue account per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: TRANSFERS BETWEEN FUNDS as they appear on the revenue side -- money moving into a fund from another fund rather than from a taxpayer or the state. `v_revenue` filtered to objects beginning 490 plus object 499900; 12 rows, FY2026 period 9.
rows.caution: This is money the town moved from one of its own pockets to another. Adding it to tax and state aid double-counts, because the same dollar is a receipt in one fund and a disbursement in the other -- and the disbursement side is not in this view. The membership test is an OBJECT-CODE PATTERN (`490%` or `499900`) written into the view, not a classification anybody published; an interfund transfer coded to another object would not appear.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, fund, fund_name, object, name, budgeted, received, still_to_come FROM v_interfund ORDER BY received DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per budget line per year, stages pivoted into columns
rows.what_it_answers: Budget against what was actually spent, one row per line per year: the `settled` budget, the `proposed` budget and the `actual` (stage `restated`) side by side, FY2014-FY2027. This is the starting point for asking which lines underspend or overspend their budget. Scenario figures are excluded -- `variant = ''` only.
rows.caution: `documents_disagree` IS WRONG AS A BUDGET-VS-ACTUAL FLAG. It is MAX() across ALL stages, so a line where two documents disagree about the PROPOSED column is reported as a line whose budget and actual are disputed. Of the disagreeing line-year-stage cells, 254 are `proposed` against 45 `settled` and 35 `restated`, and the view flags 322 of its 4,506 rows on that basis. `scripts/build_variance_charts.py` does NOT use this view: it pivots the flag PER STAGE and records that the difference moved every figure on the budget-vs-actual page by about 15%. Do the same, or read the flag from `budget_figure` with a stage filter. Separately: a NULL column is a line the documents state at only one stage, not a zero.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, line_key, label, settled, proposed, actual, settled - actual AS under_budget, documents_disagree FROM v_line_budget_vs_actual WHERE settled IS NOT NULL AND actual IS NOT NULL ORDER BY fy, under_budget DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per source document per kind of fact
rows.what_it_answers: Which DOCUMENT every money fact came out of, and how many rows it produced: the ledger rows, the budget figures and the workbook figures, each grouped by `doc_id` and joined to the document's archive path, what produced its figures (`basis`) and whether our copy still matches the publisher's (`copy_state`). The answer to 'where did this number come from' at the document level.
rows.caution: A count of ROWS, not of dollars -- a document with 1,148 figures is not therefore more authoritative than one with 12. `basis` is rule 13a's distinction (a printout from the accounting system versus a sheet somebody assembled) and it is what decides how much weight a figure carries, not the row count. `copy_state` is NULL where `verify_source_copies.py` has not checked that document. Covers the three money tables only; datasets extracted from the annual reports get their provenance from `dataset-provenance.csv` instead.
rows.default_query: SELECT fact, doc_id, path, basis, copy_state, rows FROM v_provenance ORDER BY fact, rows DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per revenue account per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: MONEY COMING IN -- every revenue account in the town's MUNIS books with the sign flipped to positive: what was budgeted, what has been received, what is still to come, and the percent received. Property tax, state aid, local receipts, fees, transfers in. FY2026 at period 9, 224 accounts.
rows.caution: THE SIGNS ARE NEGATED HERE. `ledger_snapshot` stores revenue negative and this view multiplies by -1, so figures are positive in the view and negative in the table it reads -- never mix the two in one sum. `pct_received` is computed from the RAW columns, not the negated ones. A part-year snapshot: 74.5% of the tax levy received at 31 March is the calendar, not a shortfall. `still_to_come` is the ledger's `available`, negated -- it is what has not been collected yet, not a forecast.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, fund, fund_name, object, name, budgeted, revised, received, still_to_come, pct_received FROM v_revenue ORDER BY revised DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per revenue account per year per period, with our class attached
rows.what_it_answers: Money coming in, grouped by WHERE IT COMES FROM: property tax levy, state aid, local receipts, one-time money, transfers in. `v_revenue` left-joined to our `money_classification` rows for revenue accounts. This is the view behind the revenue side of the money-flow diagrams.
rows.caution: THE CLASS IS A DEFAULT, NOT ALWAYS A MEASUREMENT. Any account with no classification row falls through to `local` / 'Local receipts' by COALESCE, and 171 of the 224 rows carry that label -- so 'Local receipts' means 'classified as local OR not classified at all' and the two cannot be told apart from this view. Join `money_classification` yourself if you need to know which. The classification is ours, recorded so it can be argued with; `how` and `why` in `money_classification` carry the basis. Amounts are the negated (positive) figures from `v_revenue`.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, class, class_label, SUM(budgeted) AS budgeted, SUM(received) AS received, COUNT(*) AS accounts FROM v_revenue_classified GROUP BY fy, period, class, class_label ORDER BY budgeted DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per town department per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: Money going out, grouped by HOW MUCH CONTROL the town has over it: assessed, bargained, committed, delegated, transfer or discretionary, with how that was established (`control_how`). Voted, revised and expended per department. 67 departments, FY2026 period 9. This is the view behind the question 'how much of the budget could the town actually change'.
rows.caution: `discretionary` IS THE RESIDUAL AND IT IS NOT A FINDING. 49 of the 67 departments carry `control = discretionary` with `control_how = residual`, which means nobody classified them -- not that the town established they are discretionary. Read `control_how` before quoting `control`. Department roll-ups only (`level = 'department'`), expense only, so this does not tie to any account-level total. The classification is ours.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, control, control_how, department, voted, revised, expended FROM v_spending_classified ORDER BY revised DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per person per year, with our classification of their printed title
rows.what_it_answers: PEOPLE -- every name the town printed in a school staff roster, FY2011-FY2025, with the school, the page, the job title exactly as printed (`role_raw`) and our classification of it into a role category and grade. This is the dataset for counting how many teachers, paraprofessionals or secretaries a school listed in a year.
rows.caution: A COUNT OF NAMES IS NOT A STAFFING LEVEL. There is NO FTE, so a 0.4 music teacher and a full-timer are one row each; NO FUNDING SOURCE, which is the question rule 11 says actually matters; no salary; and the roster is a point in time undated within the year. `role_category` and `role_grade` are OUR judgement (see `classified_by`), not the town's words -- `role_raw` is the town's words. The join to `role_classification` is a LEFT JOIN, so an unclassified title would arrive NULL; none is NULL today. `position_legacy` is the superseded column and is kept only so an older query still resolves.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, school, role_category, role_grade, COUNT(*) AS names FROM v_staff_roster GROUP BY fy, school, role_category, role_grade ORDER BY fy, school, names DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per state-aid revenue account per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: STATE AID as the town's own books record it -- Chapter 70 and the rest of the cherry sheet, budgeted against received. `v_revenue` filtered to objects beginning 45; 29 accounts, FY2026 period 9. Chapter 70 is the single account `CH 70 AID`, $9,229,410 budgeted in FY2026.
rows.caution: CHAPTER 70 IS NOT STATE AID. It is one account in this view, and the rest of the cherry sheet -- Unrestricted General Government Aid and everything else -- is not school money. Summing this view gives total state aid, which is what `model/finance.py` grows; do not call that figure Chapter 70, and do not call Chapter 70 the town's state aid. Membership is an OBJECT-CODE PATTERN (`45%`) written into the view, not a list DESE published. Figures are negated to positive by `v_revenue`, and a part-year `pct_received` is the payment calendar rather than a shortfall.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, fund, object, name, budgeted, revised, received, pct_received FROM v_state_aid ORDER BY revised DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per account per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: Money MOVED BETWEEN LINES after the budget was voted: the original appropriation, the cumulative `transfers` into or out of it, and the revised figure, per account. `moved_since_last` is meant to be the change in transfers since the previous period.
rows.caution: `moved_since_last` IS EFFECTIVELY EMPTY AND SHOULD NOT BE USED: it is non-NULL on 2 of 983 rows, because the LAG needs the same `account_id` at two periods and `ledger_snapshot` holds none -- period 9 carries the department roll-ups plus 277 accounts and period 12 carries a different 635 accounts. The two non-NULL values are duplicate rows within period 9, not a movement between periods. `transfers` itself is real and cumulative to the snapshot date, not per-period. The view does not filter `account_type`, so 224 revenue accounts are included, and their amounts are stored NEGATIVE and are not negated here as they are in `v_revenue`. It mixes department roll-ups with detail accounts -- filter `level` before summing.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, period, dept, name, original, transfers, revised, moved_since_last FROM v_transfer_history WHERE transfers <> 0 ORDER BY ABS(transfers) DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per worksheet row per year, budget column against actual column
rows.what_it_answers: Budget against actual TAKEN FROM ONE DOCUMENT -- the district's own workbook, matching a `budget` or `final_budget` column to the `actual` column on the same worksheet row, same year, same document. `under_budget` is budget minus actual. 245 lines, FY2025.
rows.caution: The join is `doc_id` AND `row` AND `fy`, so both figures come from the SAME sheet and the same printed row -- which is the like-for-like comparison, but it also means the coverage is whatever that one workbook prints, not the district's whole budget. `row_kind = 'line'` excludes subtotals, so these do not add to any printed total. `under_budget` is a difference between two columns of one document; it is not a statement about what was appropriated. And rule 13a applies: a hand-built workbook is an argument, not a printout from the books -- check `document_basis` for what produced this one.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, line_key, row, budget, actual, under_budget FROM v_workbook_budget_vs_actual ORDER BY under_budget DESC LIMIT 1000
